neighbours.label: lab-method context of counting cells or particles with an instrument (counted with the aid of a microscope, hemocytometer, counting chamber)
fire: Viable cells were counted in a Neubauer counting chamber after staining.
Spores were enumerated with the aid of a hemocytometer and a lens.
The number of cells in each well was determined using a counting chamber.
Red blood cells were counted with the aid of an improved Neubauer slide.
Leukocytes were quantified using a hemocytometer under low magnification.
Yeast cells were counted with the aid of a Thoma counting chamber.
Total sperm count was obtained using a Makler counting chamber.
Algal cells were enumerated using a Sedgewick-Rafter counting cell.
quiet: Viable cells were stained with trypan blue before the experiment.
Spores were collected from the plates and stored at four degrees.
The cells in each well were washed twice with buffer.
Red blood cells were separated from plasma by centrifugation.
Leukocytes were incubated overnight in culture medium.
Yeast cells were grown in rich medium at thirty degrees.
The semen samples were collected after three days of abstinence.
Algal cultures were kept under constant light for a week.

notes: Card top examples are mixed (eight plots, '> 0', × 8,000/200, Counting Chamber). Probe: 'counted with the aid of a microscope' 0.70 and 'hemocytometer' 0.46; generic measuring/counting sentences stay low. The opposite pole is the micro sign (µ, μ, micro).
